Eleventh Indian Expedition to Antarctica Scientific Report, 1995 
Department of Ocean Development, Technical Publication. No. 9, pp. 121-144 
B.R.BEJARNIYA.V.RAVIKANT, S.MUKERJI, S.C.NAUTIYAL, 
L.K.OBEROI and A.S.GILL 
Geological Survey of India. 
NH-5 P, N.I.T., Faridabad -121 001 
Abstract 
Introduction 
Payer-Weyprecht Mountains and  associated nunataks  are  exposed about 
80 km southeast  of Gruber massif (Wohlthat mountains) in the Central Dron-
ning Maud  Land ,East Antarctica (Fig 1). The outcrop free area  between the 
two mountain  ranges  is  occupied  by  thick  continental  ice  sheet.  Geological 
mapping of  these distant  mountains  covering  an  area  bounded  by  latitudes 
71°49'36" & 72°05'48"S and longitudes 13°09'34" & 14°49'27"E, was under-
taken during the eleventh Indian expedition to Antarctica. 
Geology 
Regional geological setting : 
There is  hardly  any  geological  information  available  from  Payer-
Weyprecht region, however, the adjoining Wohlthat mountains are fairly well 
studied (Ravich  and  Kamenev,  1975,  Kaul  et  al.,1988,Ravindra et  al., 1989, 
Joshi and  Bejarniya, 1990). The geological account of Schirmacher hill range 
which lies  further  about  90 km  north  of  Wohlthat mountains  has  also  been 
attended to in  detail  by  Kaul  et  al.(1985),  Singh  (1986)  and  Sengupta 
Geology of  the Payer-Weyprecht Mountains, Central 
Dronning Maud Laud, East Antarctica 
Orthogneiss with tabular to lensoid pyroxene-amphibolite enclaves, is exposed in the 
ice-free areas of Payer and Weyprecht Mountains. Orthogneiss was emplaced late syntec-
tonic to D2 deformation under amphibolite facies conditions which imparted a homogeneous 
foliation. The field relations and geochemical parameters suggest an I-type affinity for the 
granitic orthogneiss, while the pyroxene-amphibolite enclaves are metamorphosed products 
of basic igneous rocks.

(1988,1993). All  these  studies  have  indicated  the  presence  of  a paragneissic 
complex with  interlayered  orthogneiss  and  mafic  granulite.  This  gneissic 
complex has  undergone  multiphase  tectdnothermal  events  (Joshi  et  al., 
1991a,Sengupta op.cit.)  and  is  intruded  by  anorthosite,  monzogabbro/mon-
zonite and  many plutons of post-tectonic alkali granite.  The  alkali  granite  has 
been inferred  to  have  A-type  affinity  and  probably  manifest  a  Pan-African 
thermal event  (Joshi  et  al.,1991b, Joshi  and  Pant,  1994). Paucity  of  geochro-
nological data  from  this  region does not enable  assignment  of exact ages, but 
on the  basis  of  extrapolation  of  data from  adjoining  regions  having  similar 
lithology and tectonothermal history, a mid-Proterozoic age has been suggested 
(James and Tingey,1983). 
In the  Payer-Weyprecht  mountains,  a  quartzofeldspathic  biotite-horn-
blende gneiss is a dominant rock type containing enclaves of pyroxene-amphi-
bolite, which  is  occasionally garnetiferous.

Geology of the Payer-Weyprecht Mountains

Field characteristics and relations: 
Gneiss is homogeneously  foliated (Fig 2), the  foliation being defined by 
the preferred shape orientation of biotite and hornblende. Composition layering 
is variably  developed. In  contrast  the  mafic  enclaves which are  layered and 
foliated, occur  as discontinuous tabular bodies and boudins of variable dimen-
sions with sharp but occasionally sheared contacts. Mutual angularity between 
foliation in  gneiss and those within enclaves is generally absent. Gneiss is free 
from any  intercalation  with  metasedimentary  rock  throughout  its  exposure. 
Foliated apophyses and  veins invading pyroxene amphibolite enclaves at the 
contact indicate an intrusive nature of the former (Figs 3,4b & 4d). The intrusive 
nature is further  strengthened by absence of an early isoclinal phase of folding 
in gneiss which is present in the amphibolite enclaves. The mafic enclaves show 
well preserved  layering  and  isoclinal  rootless  folds  (Fig 4a) indicative  of an 
earlier tectonothermal  event.  Four  sets  of  pegmatite/granite veins  have  been 
profusely injected into these rocks under brittle ductile conditions (Fig 4c). 
Petrography: 
Orthogneiss: It is a medium-grained, leuco- to mesocratic and  uniformly 
foliated rock. The  mineral  assemblage recorded  is  — Quartz-orthoclase  & 
microciine perthites-oligoclase-hornblende- biotite-zircon-sphene-garnet.
